question_type: multi-issue aggregation (geometric mean of 4 component columns x 4 July rows of table IFS-1) with one revised cell; vintage-disputed key
decisive_step: Vintage of one cell: the July-2011 'Reserve position in IMF' value of table IFS-1. Its first printing (treasury_bulletin_2011_09.txt:1990) differs from the revised printing ('July r' in treasury_bulletin_2011_12.txt:2598, carried unchanged through treasury_bulletin_2012_09.txt:2003; footnote 6 at 2012_09:2023 explains the revision). Every other of the 16 cells is identical in all printings. The reference solution chose the latest revision (worklog 'Decision on vintage'; solution.json decisions[1]) and was graded wrong; the only cell that was graded right (b2) used the first printing, so the answer key follows the September-issue (first-print) value. issue47 = true: the key is publicly disputed.

a.path_summary: a[4] find_tables found IFS-1; a[6] show_table of the 2013_12 issue showed the five columns and the July-2013 row; a[8] and a[10] ran printings in a shell loop for each of the 4 components x 4 Julys (32 calls) and read the SUMMARY lines, which showed the July-2011 IMF cell as 'REVISED/DIFFERS across printings' with a later value; a[11] chose the latest value for every cell per the text and a[12] computed the geometric mean with calc. Same value as b, c and the reference.

first_divergence.what_it_did: Took the revised (Dec-2011 onward) printing of the July-2011 IMF reserve-position cell, following the 'use the latest printing' rule of AGENTS.md.
first_divergence.what_a_right_cell_or_the_reference_did: b2 (graded right) used the first printing from the 2011_09 issue (via show_table of that issue, b2[16]), without knowing a revision existed. The reference made the same choice as a and was graded wrong.

tool_use.friction: a[4] find_tables output cut at 8000 bytes (356 groups for a 3-word query); a[8] the 16-call printings loop was truncated in the middle (~15 KB omitted), so a[10] re-ran 8 of the calls with tail -8 to recover the 2011/2012 summaries. No errors.

a.text_use: acted on 'Bulletins revise earlier numbers ... use the latest printing of each value' (a[5] 'Need latest printing for each July', a[7]); also 'Compute every final number with calc' (a[12]).

b.path_summary: b[6] find_tables --all was cut at 8000 bytes; b[8] misused show_table with line 0 --match and got the Contents table; b[10]/[12] narrowed by --years and displayed the 2013_12 table with --stitch; b[15]-[16] reasoned (wrongly, but harmlessly) that each July's latest printing is the same-year September issue, then b[17] displayed the 2010_09, 2011_09 and 2012_09 tables; the 2012_09 table carries the revised July-2011 row, and b[18] explicitly chose that revision over the first print it had seen. b[19] calc, b[21] submit.

first_divergence.what_it_did: Chose the revised July-2011 IMF value from the 2012_09 issue over the first print in the 2011_09 issue ('latest revision ... due revision'), without any advice text telling it to.
first_divergence.what_a_right_cell_or_the_reference_did: b2 used the 2011_09 first print. The reference chose the revision, like b.

tool_use.friction: b[6] --all output cut at 8000 bytes; b[8] show_table <file> 0 --match matched the Contents table instead of IFS-1 (wasted step); b[17] three show_table calls in one command, the digest shows only the last table (the earlier two were pushed out of the clipped output).

b.text_use: none (no advice text in this cell)
b.harness_use: Gate round 1 (call 9): rule row_coverage fired: 'Your sum uses 3 cells of row treasury_bulletin_2011_09.txt:1978 (2010-07); 1 other cells of that row are unused, e.g. Gold stock'. False positive: the gold-stock value is identical in every row, so the binder attached that cell elsewhere and counted only 3 of the 4 used cells; also the answer is a geometric mean, not a sum. No offer. b[22] puzzled over it, b[23] kept with a reason; recorded. Did not change the answer. No later_printing finding (the answer already used the latest printing).

b2.path_summary: b2[6] find_tables, b2[9] show_table 2013_12 July row, then b2[12] the same 16-call printings loop as a but with --years; the model reported the output truncated in the middle (the 2011 and 2012 blocks, including the REVISED summary for the July-2011 IMF cell, were the part it could not see). b2[14] show_table 2013_12 --long for July 2013, b2[16] show_table of the 2012_09 and 2011_09 issues with --grep for July 2012 and July 2011: the 2011_09 issue is the first printing of July 2011, so b2 used the pre-revision value without knowing a revision existed. b2[19] calc, b2[21] submit, recorded with no finding.

first_divergence.what_it_did: Intended the latest printing (b2[7], b2[10], b2[11] 'pulling the latest printed value for each July') but, after the printings loop truncated, took the July-2011 row from the 2011_09 issue, which is the first printing. Right by luck: its stated policy was the same as a/b/c.
first_divergence.what_a_right_cell_or_the_reference_did: n/a (this is the cell graded right); the reference and a/b/c took the revised printing.

tool_use.friction: b2[6] find_tables cut at 8000 bytes; b2[12] 16 printings calls in one command, output truncated in the middle (model: 'Output truncated missing 2011 and 2012 some'), which hid the only REVISED summary; b2[16] passed the last line of the table (2015/1978) instead of its first line and show_table still resolved the table (tolerant).

b2.text_use: acted on 'use the latest printing of each value: for every table cell you use, run printings' (b2[10]-[12]) but could not complete it after truncation; 'Compute every final number with calc' (b2[19]).
b2.harness_use: Submit at call 8: recorded, no finding, gate_rounds 0. The later_printing rule (in b2's 5-rule set, offer=substitute_printing) did NOT fire although a later printing of the July-2011 IMF cell differs from the one used; the checks file shows no finding. Had it fired and been accepted, b2 would have been graded wrong. Worth checking why it stayed silent (the differing printing was in the truncated tool output; the ledger may not have bound the cell).

c.path_summary: Same route as a at temperature 1: c[5] find_tables, c[8] show_table 2013_12 --grep July (only the 2013 row, because other rows' labels are like '2012 - Oct'), c[10] read the raw lines with sed to be sure, c[13] the 16-call printings loop (truncated), c[15] re-ran 2011/2012 with tail -n 4 and saw the REVISED summary for the July-2011 IMF cell, c[17] SAY explicitly 'applying the latest value', c[18] calc.

first_divergence.what_it_did: Saw both printings of the July-2011 IMF cell in the printings SUMMARY and chose the later revision, per the text.
first_divergence.what_a_right_cell_or_the_reference_did: b2 used the first printing; the reference chose the revision.

tool_use.friction: c[5] cut at 8000 bytes; c[8] --grep July returned one row and 'page rows 1-1 of 1', which c[9] found confusing and re-read the raw text; c[13] printings loop truncated in the middle, c[15] recovered with tail.

c.text_use: acted on 'use the latest printing of each value' (c[6] 'Need latest printing each cell', c[17]); 'Alternatives: weigh them against the question's exact wording' (c[16]-[17] weighed and chose); 'Compute every final number with calc' (c[18]).

smallest_change.change: No adapter change is justified. All three wrong cells and the reference solution identified the right table, the right 16 cells and the right formula, and applied the paper's stated vintage rule (latest revision unless a date is pinned) to the one revised cell; the key follows the first printing instead. The only change that would flip a/b/c here is 'prefer the first printing', which contradicts the convention that is right elsewhere (the later_printing rule and the AGENTS.md vintage sentence exist because of those questions).
smallest_change.could_hurt_right_cells: yes: a first-printing preference would hurt every question where the key follows a revision

alternatives.change: At submit, when any input cell of the final calc has more than one distinct printed value across issues, record the non-chosen vintage's recomputed answer as an automatic --alt in the ledger and print one line 'vintage alternative recorded: first printing of <locator> gives <value>' without an Accept offer. Does not change the graded answer; it makes vintage-disputed near-misses visible to the learner and to analysis (a, b, c and the reference would all have carried the b2 value as the alt).
alternatives.why_not_first: Does not fix correctness on this question; a bookkeeping change, useful for issue47 triage rather than for scoring.

alternatives.change: printings: accept several --col values (or --cols all) and a --summary flag that prints only the SUMMARY block per column, so a 4x4 cell sweep is one call of ~40 lines instead of 16 calls of ~15 lines each. In this pilot every cell that swept with printings (a[8], b2[12], c[13]) hit middle-of-output truncation and had to re-run or fall back to show_table; b2's fallback is what accidentally produced the graded-right value.
alternatives.why_not_first: Friction fix, not a correctness fix here: with complete output b2 would have seen the REVISED summary and, following its own stated policy, produced the same graded-wrong value as a/b/c.

alternatives.change: row_coverage rule: bind a used cell to the row the model actually printed it from (or skip the rule when the value is repeated across rows, as the gold-stock column is), and do not fire for non-additive aggregates (geometric mean, median). It fired a false positive in b (call 9).
alternatives.why_not_first: Did not change b's answer; noise reduction only.

fix.why_not_text: n/a (no fix). As evidence: cell a had the vintage sentence and followed it exactly; cell b had no text and made the same choice on its own from the printed 'r' revision; the reference made it with full deliberation (review.md section 3). The text is not what separates right from wrong here.
fix.irreducible: Yes. The question pins no issue or date; the key sides with the first printing while the documented convention (and the reference solution, graded wrong) sides with the revision. b2's correct grade is luck (truncated tool output pushed it to the September issue). issue47 is true for this question.

kept-and-helped: 'Alternatives: when two candidate values fit ... weigh them against the question's exact wording' (c[17] weighed both printings; the choice then followed the vintage sentence)

kept-and-helped: 'Several tables in one issue can look alike. Search with find_tables using the question's key nouns ... note its id so printings can follow it' (all cells noted IFS-1 and swept it with printings)
irrelevant: 'For a sum over the columns of one row, list the whole row' (a geometric mean, and the row was listed anyway)
irrelevant: 'Match the period exactly. FY ... and CY' (monthly rows, no FY/CY confusion)

notes: (1) All four cells and the reference converge on the same 16 cells and formula; the whole spread of outcomes is one cell's vintage. Any v10 scoring of this question measures the vintage convention, not the adapter. (2) Truncated multi-call printings sweeps are a recurring friction: a[8], b2[12], c[13] each lost the middle ~15 KB; the model then re-ran with tail (a, c) or switched to show_table (b2). A --summary/multi-column mode would remove three wasted steps per question of this shape. (3) b's row_coverage finding was a false positive on a repeated-value column and a non-additive aggregate. (4) b2's later_printing rule stayed silent although a later printing differed; if that is because the differing printing only appeared in truncated output, the ledger's cell binding depends on what the model happened to display, which is fragile in both directions. (5) v8: v8_none right, v8_prompt and v8_cards wrong, same pattern (no vintage advice -> September issues -> first print); the v8 per-question file referenced in index.json (per-question/036.json) is absent from the folder.
